commands.name: critical-analysis

commands.name: data-analysis

commands.name: hypothesis-generation

commands.name: literature-review

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

commands.name: simplify

commands.name: batch

Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: built-in-browser
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step that uses the built-in browser, the browser pane inside the Claude desktop app (also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or "your own browser"), whose tools are named mcp__Claude_Browser__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser tool instead. It covers the pane's persistent sign-ins, tabs and preview_start, reading pages as text, site approvals, what the pane cannot open, and what to do when it cannot be reached. It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: chrome-browser
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step that uses Claude in Chrome, the browser extension whose tools are named mcp__claude-in-chrome__* (also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser) and which acts in the person's real Chrome with their own sign-ins; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome tool instead. It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. It is not for the built-in browser (mcp__Claude_Browser__* or mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: computer-use
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for "computer use". Computer use (desktop control) lets Claude take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with clicks, typing and scrolling through the Claude desktop app; its tools are named mcp__computer-use__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__computer_* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before computer use is turned on for a conversation there may be no such tools, only an enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer tool, which turns it on. It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills. (claude.ai sync)

commands.description: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached. commands.name: docx
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: google-workspace
commands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files. (claude.ai sync)

This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill. commands.name: xlsx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. # Planning: The Chain-of-Thought Tax

## Motivation & Novelty Assessment

### Why This Research Matters
Chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting is applied almost by default, yet it costs 10-50x more output tokens than
a direct answer. If CoT also *lowers* accuracy on some task types, practitioners are paying twice. Knowing
which task categories benefit, which are taxed, and how that changes with model size lets people route
prompts sensibly instead of using CoT everywhere.

### Gap in Existing Work
No pre-gathered literature review was present in the workspace (the resource-finder stage was skipped), so
this is from my own knowledge of the literature rather than a systematic review:
- Wei et al. 2022 and Kojima et al. 2022 established CoT gains, mostly on arithmetic/symbolic tasks.
- Sprague et al. 2024 ("To CoT or not to CoT?") meta-analysed 100+ papers and found gains concentrated on
  math/symbolic tasks, with near-zero benefit elsewhere - but mostly reports "no gain", not harm.
- Liu et al. 2024 ("Mind Your Step (by Step)") show CoT *hurts* on tasks where verbal deliberation hurts
  humans (implicit pattern learning, etc.).
- Most comparisons mix model families, so "scale" is confounded with training data and recipe.

Missing: a controlled *within-family* scale ladder, with paired item-level statistics, that separates
"CoT gives no gain" from "CoT actively breaks answers the model otherwise gets right".

### Our Novel Contribution
A paired direct-vs-CoT comparison over 4 task categories x 2 datasets each, on five sizes of one model
family (Qwen2.5-Instruct 0.5B-14B, a 30x parameter range), reporting not only the accuracy delta but the
*harm rate* P(CoT wrong | direct right) and *fix rate* P(CoT right | direct wrong), which are not
distorted by ceiling effects the way raw deltas are.

### Experiment Justification
- Exp 1 (main grid: 5 models x 8 tasks x {direct, CoT}): directly tests the sign and size of the CoT
  effect per category (H1, H2).
- Exp 2 (scale trend): slope of the CoT delta against log2(parameters) per category tests the claimed
  shift of the crossover with scale (H3).
- Exp 3 (prompt-paraphrase robustness: a second CoT wording): greedy decoding has no seed variance, so
  prompt wording is the relevant nuisance variable; checks that conclusions are not one prompt's artefact.
- Exp 4 (error analysis: harm/fix rates, parse failures, truncation, reasoning length): distinguishes a
  real reasoning tax from formatting/extraction artefacts.

## Research Question
Does zero-shot CoT lower accuracy on pattern-matching and factual-recall tasks (by 5-15 points) while
raising it on logical deduction and arithmetic (by 10-25 points), and does the set of categories that
benefit shrink as model scale grows?

## Hypothesis Decomposition
- H1: For pattern matching and factual recall, delta = acc(CoT) - acc(direct) lies in [-15, -5] pp.
- H2: For logical deduction and arithmetic, delta lies in [+10, +25] pp.
- H3: As parameters increase, fewer categories show a positive delta (deltas trend downward with scale).
- (Mechanistic clause "larger models internalise reasoning that traces disrupt" is NOT directly testable
  with behavioural data; at most the results can be consistent or inconsistent with it.)
"5-15%" is read as percentage points of accuracy; relative changes are reported alongside.

Independent variables: prompt condition (direct / CoT), task category, model size.
Dependent variable: item-level correctness (0/1).

## Proposed Methodology

### Approach
The environment has no API key (OPENROUTER_KEY and all provider keys are unset), so API models are not
available. Instead I run real open-weight models locally on the 4x RTX A6000. This is a deviation from the
default instruction, but it gives a cleaner test of the scale claim: one family, one training recipe, five
sizes. Models: Qwen2.5-{0.5B, 1.5B, 3B, 7B, 14B}-Instruct (already in the local HF cache; larger sizes are
not cached and the data disk has ~6 GB free, so 14B is the ceiling).

### Tasks (n = 300 items each, fixed seed 42)
| Category | Task | Source | Format |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pattern matching | AG News topic | fancyzhx/ag_news test | 4 labels |
| Pattern matching | SST-2 sentiment | stanfordnlp/sst2 validation | 2 labels |
| Factual recall | TriviaQA | rc.nocontext validation | free-form, alias match |
| Factual recall | MMLU recall-heavy subjects | cais/mmlu test | 4-way MCQ |
| Logical deduction | BBH logical_deduction_five_objects | lukaemon/bbh (250 items, all used) | 5-way MCQ |
| Logical deduction | ProofWriter OWA depth-5 | tasksource/proofwriter validation | True/False/Unknown |
| Arithmetic | GSM8K | openai/gsm8k test | number |
| Arithmetic | Synthetic multi-step arithmetic | generated here (contamination-free) | number |

### Conditions
- Direct: instruction to give only the answer; the assistant turn is prefilled with "Answer:" and capped
  at 24 new tokens, so the model cannot reason in the output.
- CoT: "think step by step", then a final "Answer: ..." line; 640 new tokens.
- CoT-v2 (robustness): a differently worded reasoning instruction.
Zero-shot, greedy decoding (temperature 0), default system prompt, identical items across conditions.

### Baselines
Direct answering is the baseline for CoT. Chance levels per task are reported (25%, 50%, 20%, 33%, ~0%).

### Evaluation Metrics
Accuracy; paired delta (CoT - direct); harm rate; fix rate; parse-failure and truncation rates; output
tokens (the literal cost side of the "tax").

### Statistical Analysis Plan (fixed before seeing results)
- Per model x task and per model x category: paired bootstrap 95% CI on delta (10,000 resamples of items),
  exact McNemar test, Holm correction across the family of tests at alpha = 0.05.
- H1/H2 are judged per model x category: supported if the point estimate is inside the stated band and the
  CI excludes 0 in the predicted direction.
- H3: OLS slope of category delta on log2(params), CI by item bootstrap; plus the count of categories/tasks
  with a significantly positive delta at each size.
- CoT answers with no parsable final answer count as wrong (reported separately, with a sensitivity
  analysis that excludes them).

## Expected Outcomes
Support: negative deltas on classification/recall, positive on logic/arithmetic, positive deltas shrinking
with size. Refutation: deltas near zero or positive on recall/pattern tasks; no monotone scale trend.

## Timeline
Setup and data 30 min; harness + pilot 40 min; full runs ~60 min on 4 GPUs; analysis 40 min; report 30 min.

## Potential Challenges
- Small models ignoring the output format -> track parse failures, sensitivity analysis.
- Ceiling effects on SST-2 -> harm/fix rates.
- Truncated CoT -> 640-token budget, report truncation rate.
- Disk nearly full -> venv symlinked to the uv cache, only small parquet files downloaded.

## Success Criteria
All 5 models x 8 tasks x 2 conditions completed with item-level outputs saved; each sub-hypothesis gets an
explicit supported / not supported verdict with CIs.

# Planning: The Chain-of-Thought Tax

## Motivation & Novelty Assessment

### Why This Research Matters
Chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting is applied almost by default, yet it costs 10-50x more output tokens than
a direct answer. If CoT also *lowers* accuracy on some task types, practitioners are paying twice. Knowing
which task categories benefit, which are taxed, and how that changes with model size lets people route
prompts sensibly instead of using CoT everywhere.

### Gap in Existing Work
No pre-gathered literature review was present in the workspace (the resource-finder stage was skipped), so
this is from my own knowledge of the literature rather than a systematic review:
- Wei et al. 2022 and Kojima et al. 2022 established CoT gains, mostly on arithmetic/symbolic tasks.
- Sprague et al. 2024 ("To CoT or not to CoT?") meta-analysed 100+ papers and found gains concentrated on
  math/symbolic tasks, with near-zero benefit elsewhere - but mostly reports "no gain", not harm.
- Liu et al. 2024 ("Mind Your Step (by Step)") show CoT *hurts* on tasks where verbal deliberation hurts
  humans (implicit pattern learning, etc.).
- Most comparisons mix model families, so "scale" is confounded with training data and recipe.

Missing: a controlled *within-family* scale ladder, with paired item-level statistics, that separates
"CoT gives no gain" from "CoT actively breaks answers the model otherwise gets right".

### Our Novel Contribution
A paired direct-vs-CoT comparison over 4 task categories x 2 datasets each, on five sizes of one model
family (Qwen2.5-Instruct 0.5B-14B, a 30x parameter range), reporting not only the accuracy delta but the
*harm rate* P(CoT wrong | direct right) and *fix rate* P(CoT right | direct wrong), which are not
distorted by ceiling effects the way raw deltas are.

### Experiment Justification
- Exp 1 (main grid: 5 models x 8 tasks x {direct, CoT}): directly tests the sign and size of the CoT
  effect per category (H1, H2).
- Exp 2 (scale trend): slope of the CoT delta against log2(parameters) per category tests the claimed
  shift of the crossover with scale (H3).
- Exp 3 (prompt-paraphrase robustness: a second CoT wording): greedy decoding has no seed variance, so
  prompt wording is the relevant nuisance variable; checks that conclusions are not one prompt's artefact.
- Exp 4 (error analysis: harm/fix rates, parse failures, truncation, reasoning length): distinguishes a
  real reasoning tax from formatting/extraction artefacts.

## Research Question
Does zero-shot CoT lower accuracy on pattern-matching and factual-recall tasks (by 5-15 points) while
raising it on logical deduction and arithmetic (by 10-25 points), and does the set of categories that
benefit shrink as model scale grows?

## Hypothesis Decomposition
- H1: For pattern matching and factual recall, delta = acc(CoT) - acc(direct) lies in [-15, -5] pp.
- H2: For logical deduction and arithmetic, delta lies in [+10, +25] pp.
- H3: As parameters increase, fewer categories show a positive delta (deltas trend downward with scale).
- (Mechanistic clause "larger models internalise reasoning that traces disrupt" is NOT directly testable
  with behavioural data; at most the results can be consistent or inconsistent with it.)
"5-15%" is read as percentage points of accuracy; relative changes are reported alongside.

Independent variables: prompt condition (direct / CoT), task category, model size.
Dependent variable: item-level correctness (0/1).

## Proposed Methodology

### Approach
The environment has no API key (OPENROUTER_KEY and all provider keys are unset), so API models are not
available. Instead I run real open-weight models locally on the 4x RTX A6000. This is a deviation from the
default instruction, but it gives a cleaner test of the scale claim: one family, one training recipe, five
sizes. Models: Qwen2.5-{0.5B, 1.5B, 3B, 7B, 14B}-Instruct (already in the local HF cache; larger sizes are
not cached and the data disk has ~6 GB free, so 14B is the ceiling).

### Tasks (n = 300 items each, fixed seed 42)
| Category | Task | Source | Format |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pattern matching | AG News topic | fancyzhx/ag_news test | 4 labels |
| Pattern matching | SST-2 sentiment | stanfordnlp/sst2 validation | 2 labels |
| Factual recall | TriviaQA | rc.nocontext validation | free-form, alias match |
| Factual recall | MMLU recall-heavy subjects | cais/mmlu test | 4-way MCQ |
| Logical deduction | BBH logical_deduction_five_objects | lukaemon/bbh (250 items, all used) | 5-way MCQ |
| Logical deduction | ProofWriter OWA depth-5 | tasksource/proofwriter validation | True/False/Unknown |
| Arithmetic | GSM8K | openai/gsm8k test | number |
| Arithmetic | Synthetic multi-step arithmetic | generated here (contamination-free) | number |

### Conditions
- Direct: instruction to give only the answer; the assistant turn is prefilled with "Answer:" and capped
  at 24 new tokens, so the model cannot reason in the output.
- CoT: "think step by step", then a final "Answer: ..." line; 640 new tokens.
- CoT-v2 (robustness): a differently worded reasoning instruction.
Zero-shot, greedy decoding (temperature 0), default system prompt, identical items across conditions.

### Baselines
Direct answering is the baseline for CoT. Chance levels per task are reported (25%, 50%, 20%, 33%, ~0%).

### Evaluation Metrics
Accuracy; paired delta (CoT - direct); harm rate; fix rate; parse-failure and truncation rates; output
tokens (the literal cost side of the "tax").

### Statistical Analysis Plan (fixed before seeing results)
- Per model x task and per model x category: paired bootstrap 95% CI on delta (10,000 resamples of items),
  exact McNemar test, Holm correction across the family of tests at alpha = 0.05.
- H1/H2 are judged per model x category: supported if the point estimate is inside the stated band and the
  CI excludes 0 in the predicted direction.
- H3: OLS slope of category delta on log2(params), CI by item bootstrap; plus the count of categories/tasks

with size. Refutation: deltas near zero or positive on recall/pattern tasks; no monotone scale trend.

"""Build the fixed evaluation set: 8 tasks in 4 categories, written to datasets/processed/tasks.jsonl.

Each record: id, task, category, text (task-specific question incl. answer-format hint),
answer_type (label | mcq | number | freeform), gold (str or list of aliases), labels (for label tasks).
"""
import glob
import json
import os
import random

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

SEED = 42
N = 300
HF_HUB = os.path.join(os.environ.get("HF_HOME", os.path.expanduser("~/.cache/huggingface")), "hub")
RAW = "datasets/raw"
OUT = "datasets/processed/tasks.jsonl"
LETTERS = "ABCDE"

# MMLU subjects that are dominated by fact retrieval rather than multi-step reasoning.
MMLU_RECALL_SUBJECTS = [
    "miscellaneous", "world_religions", "high_school_geography", "prehistory",
    "anatomy", "nutrition", "astronomy",
]


def cached(pattern):
    """Resolve a parquet file inside the shared HF hub cache."""
    hits = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(HF_HUB, pattern)))
    assert hits, f"not found in HF cache: {pattern}"
    return hits[0]


def sample(df, n, seed=SEED):
    return df.sample(n=min(n, len(df)), random_state=seed).reset_index(drop=True)


def ag_news():
    df = sample(pd.read_parquet(cached("datasets--fancyzhx--ag_news/snapshots/*/data/test-*.parquet")), N)
    labels = ["World", "Sports", "Business", "Sci/Tech"]
    for i, r in df.iterrows():
        yield dict(id=f"agnews-{i}", task="ag_news", category="pattern_matching", answer_type="label",
                   labels=labels, gold=labels[int(r["label"])],
                   text=f"Classify the topic of this news article.\n\nArticle: {r['text']}\n\n"
                        f"The answer must be exactly one of: World, Sports, Business, Sci/Tech.")


def sst2():
    df = sample(pd.read_parquet(f"{RAW}/stanfordnlp__sst2/data/validation-00000-of-00001.parquet"), N)
    labels = ["negative", "positive"]
    for i, r in df.iterrows():
        yield dict(id=f"sst2-{i}", task="sst2", category="pattern_matching", answer_type="label",
                   labels=labels, gold=labels[int(r["label"])],
                   text=f"Classify the sentiment of this movie review sentence.\n\nSentence: {r['sentence'].strip()}\n\n"
                        f"The answer must be exactly one of: positive, negative.")


def triviaqa():
    df = pd.read_parquet(f"{RAW}/mandarjoshi__trivia_qa/rc.nocontext/validation-00000-of-00001.parquet")
    df = sample(df.drop_duplicates("question"), N)
    for i, r in df.iterrows():
        aliases = sorted(set(list(r["answer"]["normalized_aliases"]) + [r["answer"]["normalized_value"]]))
        yield dict(id=f"triviaqa-{i}", task="triviaqa", category="factual_recall", answer_type="freeform",
                   gold=aliases,
                   text=f"Answer this trivia question.\n\nQuestion: {r['question']}\n\n"
                        f"The answer should be a short name or phrase.")


def mmlu():
    df = pd.read_parquet(cached("datasets--cais--mmlu/snapshots/*/all/test-*.parquet"))
    df = sample(df[df["subject"].isin(MMLU_RECALL_SUBJECTS)], N)
    for i, r in df.iterrows():
        opts = "\n".join(f"({LETTERS[j]}) {c}" for j, c in enumerate(r["choices"]))
        yield dict(id=f"mmlu-{i}", task="mmlu_recall", category="factual_recall", answer_type="mcq",
                   gold=LETTERS[int(r["answer"])], n_options=4, subject=r["subject"],
                   text=f"Answer this multiple-choice question.\n\nQuestion: {r['question']}\n{opts}\n\n"
                        f"The answer must be a single letter: A, B, C, or D.")


def bbh_logic():
    df = pd.read_parquet(f"{RAW}/lukaemon__bbh/logical_deduction_five_objects/test-00000-of-00001.parquet")
    df = sample(df, N)  # only 250 items exist; all are used
    for i, r in df.iterrows():
        yield dict(id=f"bbhlogic-{i}", task="bbh_logical_deduction", category="logical_deduction",
                   answer_type="mcq", gold=r["target"].strip("()"), n_options=5,
                   text=f"{r['input']}\n\nThe answer must be a single letter: A, B, C, D, or E.")


def proofwriter():
    df = pd.read_parquet(glob.glob(f"{RAW}/tasksource__proofwriter/data/validation-*.parquet")[0])
    # Open-world, depth-5 theories; keep questions that need >=1 inference step (or are Unknown).
    df = df[(df["config"] == "depth-5") & df["id"].str.contains("OWA")]
    df = df[(df["answer"] == "Unknown") | (df["QDep"].astype(str).isin(["1", "2", "3", "4", "5"]))]
    parts = [sample(df[df["answer"] == a], N // 3, seed=SEED + k) for k, a in enumerate(["True", "False", "Unknown"])]
    df = pd.concat(parts).sample(frac=1, random_state=SEED).reset_index(drop=True)
    labels = ["True", "False", "Unknown"]
    for i, r in df.iterrows():
        yield dict(id=f"proofwriter-{i}", task="proofwriter", category="logical_deduction", answer_type="label",
                   labels=labels, gold=r["answer"], qdep=str(r["QDep"]),
                   text=f"Here are some facts and rules:\n{r['theory']}\n\n"
                        f"Based only on the facts and rules above, is the following statement True, False, or "
                        f"Unknown (cannot be determined)?\nStatement: {r['question']}\n\n"
                        f"The answer must be exactly one of: True, False, Unknown.")


def gsm8k():
    df = sample(pd.read_parquet(cached("datasets--openai--gsm8k/snapshots/*/main/test-*.parquet")), N)
    for i, r in df.iterrows():
        gold = r["answer"].split("####")[-1].strip().replace(",", "")
        yield dict(id=f"gsm8k-{i}", task="gsm8k", category="arithmetic", answer_type="number", gold=gold,
                   text=f"Solve this math problem.\n\nProblem: {r['question']}\n\nThe answer must be a single number.")


def synth_arith():
    """Freshly generated 3-operation integer expressions, e.g. (47 * 23) + 618 - 95."""
    rng = random.Random(SEED)
    for i in range(N):
        a, b = rng.randint(12, 99), rng.randint(12, 99)
        c, d = rng.randint(100, 999), rng.randint(100, 999)
        form = rng.choice(["mul_add_sub", "add_mul", "mul_sub_mul"])
        if form == "mul_add_sub":
            expr, val = f"({a} * {b}) + {c} - {d}", a * b + c - d
        elif form == "add_mul":
            e = rng.randint(3, 9)
            expr, val = f"({c} + {d}) * {e} - {a}", (c + d) * e - a
        else:
            e, f = rng.randint(3, 9), rng.randint(3, 9)
            expr, val = f"({a} * {b}) - ({e} * {f}) + {c}", a * b - e * f + c
        yield dict(id=f"syntharith-{i}", task="synthetic_arithmetic", category="arithmetic",
                   answer_type="number", gold=str(val),
                   text=f"Compute the value of this expression.\n\n{expr}\n\nThe answer must be a single integer.")


def main():
    random.seed(SEED)
    np.random.seed(SEED)
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(OUT), exist_ok=True)
    rows = []
    for gen in [ag_news, sst2, triviaqa, mmlu, bbh_logic, proofwriter, gsm8k, synth_arith]:
        part = list(gen())
        rows += part
        golds = pd.Series([str(r["gold"]) if not isinstance(r["gold"], list) else "<aliases>" for r in part])
        print(f"{part[0]['task']:28s} n={len(part):4d}  gold dist: {golds.value_counts().head(6).to_dict()}")
    assert len({r["id"] for r in rows}) == len(rows)
    with open(OUT, "w") as f:
        for r in rows:
            f.write(json.dumps(r) + "\n")
    print(f"wrote {len(rows)} items -> {OUT}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    labels = ["World", "Sports", "Business", "Sci/Tech"]
    for i, r in df.iterrows():
        yield dict(id=f"agnews-{i}", task="ag_news", category="pattern_matching", answer_type="label",
                   labels=labels, gold=labels[int(r["label"])],
                   text=f"Classify the topic of this news article.\n\nArticle: {r['text']}\n\n"
                        f"The answer must be exactly one of: World, Sports, Business, Sci/Tech.")


def sst2():
    df = sample(pd.read_parquet(f"{RAW}/stanfordnlp__sst2/data/validation-00000-of-00001.parquet"), N)
    labels = ["negative", "positive"]
    for i, r in df.iterrows():
        yield dict(id=f"sst2-{i}", task="sst2", category="pattern_matching", answer_type="label",
                   labels=labels, gold=labels[int(r["label"])],
                   text=f"Classify the sentiment of this movie review sentence.\n\nSentence: {r['sentence'].strip()}\n\n"
                        f"The answer must be exactly one of: positive, negative.")


def triviaqa():
    df = pd.read_parquet(f"{RAW}/mandarjoshi__trivia_qa/rc.nocontext/validation-00000-of-00001.parquet")
    df = sample(df.drop_duplicates("question"), N)
    for i, r in df.iterrows():
        aliases = sorted(set(list(r["answer"]["normalized_aliases"]) + [r["answer"]["normalized_value"]]))
        yield dict(id=f"triviaqa-{i}", task="triviaqa", category="factual_recall", answer_type="freeform",
                   gold=aliases,
                   text=f"Answer this trivia question.\n\nQuestion: {r['question']}\n\n"
                        f"The answer should be a short name or phrase.")


def mmlu():
    df = pd.read_parquet(cached("datasets--cais--mmlu/snapshots/*/all/test-*.parquet"))
    df = sample(df[df["subject"].isin(MMLU_RECALL_SUBJECTS)], N)
    for i, r in df.iterrows():
        opts = "\n".join(f"({LETTERS[j]}) {c}" for j, c in enumerate(r["choices"]))
        yield dict(id=f"mmlu-{i}", task="mmlu_recall", category="factual_recall", answer_type="mcq",
                   gold=LETTERS[int(r["answer"])], n_options=4, subject=r["subject"],
                   text=f"Answer this multiple-choice question.\n\nQuestion: {r['question']}\n{opts}\n\n"
                        f"The answer must be a single letter: A, B, C, or D.")


def bbh_logic():
    df = pd.read_parquet(f"{RAW}/lukaemon__bbh/logical_deduction_five_objects/test-00000-of-00001.parquet")
    df = sample(df, N)  # only 250 items exist; all are used
    for i, r in df.iterrows():
        yield dict(id=f"bbhlogic-{i}", task="bbh_logical_deduction", category="logical_deduction",
                   answer_type="mcq", gold=r["target"].strip("()"), n_options=5,
                   text=f"{r['input']}\n\nThe answer must be a single letter: A, B, C, D, or E.")


def proofwriter():
    df = pd.read_parquet(glob.glob(f"{RAW}/tasksource__proofwriter/data/validation-*.parquet")[0])
    # Open-world, depth-5 theories; keep questions that need >=1 inference step (or are Unknown).
    df = df[(df["config"] == "depth-5") & df["id"].str.contains("OWA")]
    df = df[(df["answer"] == "Unknown") | (df["QDep"].astype(str).isin(["1", "2", "3", "4", "5"]))]
    parts = [sample(df[df["answer"] == a], N // 3, seed=SEED + k) for k, a in enumerate(["True", "False", "Unknown"])]
    df = pd.concat(parts).sample(frac=1, random_state=SEED).reset_index(drop=True)
    labels = ["True", "False", "Unknown"]
    for i, r in df.iterrows():
        yield dict(id=f"proofwriter-{i}", task="proofwriter", category="logical_deduction", answer_type="label",
                   labels=labels, gold=r["answer"], qdep=str(r["QDep"]),
                   text=f"Here are some facts and rules:\n{r['theory']}\n\n"
                        f"Based only on the facts and rules above, is the following statement True, False, or "
                        f"Unknown (cannot be determined)?\nStatement: {r['question']}\n\n"
                        f"The answer must be exactly one of: True, False, Unknown.")


def gsm8k():
    df = sample(pd.read_parquet(cached("datasets--openai--gsm8k/snapshots/*/main/test-*.parquet")), N)
    for i, r in df.iterrows():
        gold = r["answer"].split("####")[-1].strip().replace(",", "")
        yield dict(id=f"gsm8k-{i}", task="gsm8k", category="arithmetic", answer_type="number", gold=gold,
                   text=f"Solve this math problem.\n\nProblem: {r['question']}\n\nThe answer must be a single number.")


def synth_arith():
    """Freshly generated 3-operation integer expressions, e.g. (47 * 23) + 618 - 95."""
    rng = random.Random(SEED)
    for i in range(N):
        a, b = rng.randint(12, 99), rng.randint(12, 99)
        c, d = rng.randint(100, 999), rng.randint(100, 999)
        form = rng.choice(["mul_add_sub", "add_mul", "mul_sub_mul"])
        if form == "mul_add_sub":
            expr, val = f"({a} * {b}) + {c} - {d}", a * b + c - d
        elif form == "add_mul":
            e = rng.randint(3, 9)
            expr, val = f"({c} + {d}) * {e} - {a}", (c + d) * e - a
        else:
            e, f = rng.randint(3, 9), rng.randint(3, 9)
            expr, val = f"({a} * {b}) - ({e} * {f}) + {c}", a * b - e * f + c
        yield dict(id=f"syntharith-{i}", task="synthetic_arithmetic", category="arithmetic",
                   answer_type="number", gold=str(val),
                   text=f"Compute the value of this expression.\n\n{expr}\n\nThe answer must be a single integer.")


def main():
    random.seed(SEED)
    np.random.seed(SEED)
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(OUT), exist_ok=True)
    rows = []
    for gen in [ag_news, sst2, triviaqa, mmlu, bbh_logic, proofwriter, gsm8k, synth_arith]:
        part = list(gen())
        rows += part
        golds = pd.Series([str(r["gold"]) if not isinstance(r["gold"], list) else "<aliases>" for r in part])
        print(f"{part[0]['task']:28s} n={len(part):4d}  gold dist: {golds.value_counts().head(6).to_dict()}")
    assert len({r["id"] for r in rows}) == len(rows)
    with open(OUT, "w") as f:
        for r in rows:
            f.write(json.dumps(r) + "\n")
    print(f"wrote {len(rows)} items -> {OUT}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Prompt templates, answer extraction and scoring shared by inference and analysis."""
import re
import string

DIRECT_SUFFIX = ('Give only the final answer, with no explanation or reasoning. '
                 'Respond in the format "Answer: <answer>".')
COT_SUFFIX = ('Think step by step and write out your reasoning. '
              'Then finish with a final line in the format "Answer: <answer>".')
# Paraphrased reasoning instruction used for the prompt-robustness check.
COT2_SUFFIX = ('Before answering, carefully work through the problem and explain your thought process. '
               'When you are done, end your response with one last line of the form "Answer: <answer>".')

CONDITIONS = {
    # name: (prompt suffix, assistant prefill, max_new_tokens)
    "direct": (DIRECT_SUFFIX, "Answer:", 24),
    "cot": (COT_SUFFIX, "", 640),
    "cot2": (COT2_SUFFIX, "", 640),
}


def build_user_prompt(item, condition):
    return f"{item['text']}\n\n{CONDITIONS[condition][0]}"


def extract_answer(output, condition):
    """Return (answer_segment, has_marker).

    Direct outputs are a continuation of the prefilled "Answer:", so the whole output is the answer.
    CoT outputs: text after the LAST "Answer:" marker; if there is none, fall back to the last
    non-empty line and flag the response as lacking the marker.
    """
    out = output.strip()
    if condition == "direct":
        return out.split("\n")[0].strip(), True
    hits = list(re.finditer(r"answer\s*:", out, flags=re.I))
    if hits:
        seg = out[hits[-1].end():].strip()
        return (seg.split("\n")[0].strip() if seg else ""), True
    lines = [l for l in out.split("\n") if l.strip()]
    return (lines[-1].strip() if lines else ""), False


def _norm(s):
    """TriviaQA-style normalisation: lowercase, drop punctuation/articles, squeeze whitespace."""
    s = s.lower()
    s = "".join(ch if ch not in set(string.punctuation + "‘’´`_") else " " for ch in s)
    s = re.sub(r"\b(a|an|the)\b", " ", s)
    return " ".join(s.split())


def _last_number(s):
    s = s.replace(",", "").replace("$", "")
    nums = re.findall(r"-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?", s)
    return float(nums[-1]) if nums else None


def score(item, answer):
    """Return 1 if the extracted answer segment is correct for this item, else 0."""
    t = item["answer_type"]
    a = answer.replace("*", "").strip()
    if t == "label":
        low = a.lower()
        # exactly one of the allowed labels may appear (word-boundary match), and it must be the gold one
        found = [l for l in item["labels"] if re.search(rf"(?<![a-z]){re.escape(l.lower())}(?![a-z])", low)]
        return int(found == [item["gold"]])
    if t == "mcq":
        letters = "ABCDE"[: item["n_options"]]
        m = re.match(rf"^\(?([{letters}])\)?(?![A-Za-z])", a)
        return int(bool(m) and m.group(1) == item["gold"])
    if t == "number":
        v = _last_number(a)
        return int(v is not None and abs(v - float(item["gold"])) < 1e-4)
    if t == "freeform":
        na = _norm(a)
        return int(any(al and re.search(rf"(?<!\w){re.escape(al)}(?!\w)", na) for al in item["gold"]))
    raise ValueError(t)

    non-empty line and flag the response as lacking the marker.

    if condition == "direct":

    hits = list(re.finditer(r"answer\s*:", out, flags=re.I))
    if hits:
        seg = out[hits[-1].end():].strip()
        return (seg.split("\n")[0].strip() if seg else ""), True
    lines = [l for l in out.split("\n") if l.strip()]
    return (lines[-1].strip() if lines else ""), False


def _norm(s):
    """TriviaQA-style normalisation: lowercase, drop punctuation/articles, squeeze whitespace."""
    s = s.lower()
    s = "".join(ch if ch not in set(string.punctuation + "‘’´`_") else " " for ch in s)
    s = re.sub(r"\b(a|an|the)\b", " ", s)
    return " ".join(s.split())

    s = s.replace(",", "").replace("$", "")
    nums = re.findall(r"-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?", s)
    return float(nums[-1]) if nums else None

    """Return 1 if the extracted answer segment is correct for this item, else 0."""
    t = item["answer_type"]
    a = answer.replace("*", "").strip()
    if t == "label":
        low = a.lower()
        # exactly one of the allowed labels may appear (word-boundary match), and it must be the gold one
        found = [l for l in item["labels"] if re.search(rf"(?<![a-z]){re.escape(l.lower())}(?![a-z])", low)]

        letters = "ABCDE"[: item["n_options"]]
        m = re.match(rf"^\(?([{letters}])\)?(?![A-Za-z])", a)
        return int(bool(m) and m.group(1) == item["gold"])
    if t == "number":
        v = _last_number(a)
        return int(v is not None and abs(v - float(item["gold"])) < 1e-4)
    if t == "freeform":
        na = _norm(a)
        return int(any(al and re.search(rf"(?<!\w){re.escape(al)}(?!\w)", na) for al in item["gold"]))

def _clean(seg):
    """Strip markdown / LaTeX decoration around an answer segment."""
    seg = re.sub(r"\\\\boxed\\{([^{}]*)\\}", r"\\1", seg)
    seg = re.sub(r"\\\\text\\{([^{}]*)\\}", r"\\1", seg)
    seg = re.sub(r"\\\\[()\\[\\]]|[*`$]", "", seg)
    return seg.strip()


def extract_answer(output, condition):
    """Return (answer_segment, has_marker).

    Direct outputs are a continuation of the prefilled "Answer:", so the first line is the answer.
    CoT outputs: the first non-empty line after the LAST final-answer marker; if there is no marker,
    fall back to the last non-empty line and flag the response (has_marker=False).
    """

#!/bin/bash
# Run one model to completion on shared GPUs: wait until some GPU has enough free memory, run the
# (resumable) inference script there, and retry if it dies.
# Usage: bash src/supervise.sh <model> <need_free_MiB> <batch_size>
MODEL=$1; NEED=$2; BS=$3; NAME=$(basename $MODEL)
attempt() { # extra args for run_inference.py
  while true; do
    read GPU FREE < <(nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,memory.free --format=csv,noheader,nounits | tr -d ',' | sort -k2 -n -r | head -1)
    if [ "$FREE" -ge "$NEED" ]; then
      echo "$(date +%T) $NAME: launching on GPU $GPU ($FREE MiB free): $*" >> logs/supervise.log
      CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=$GPU python src/run_inference.py --model $MODEL --batch-size $BS "$@" >> logs/run_${NAME}.log 2>&1 && return 0
      echo "$(date +%T) $NAME: run failed, retrying" >> logs/supervise.log
    fi
    sleep 45
  done
}
attempt --conditions direct cot
attempt --conditions cot2 --limit 100
echo "$(date +%T) $NAME: ALL DONE" >> logs/supervise.log
EOF
nohup setsid bash src/supervise.sh Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct 12000 64 > /dev/null 2>&1 &
sleep 1; nohup setsid bash src/supervise.sh Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct 24000 64 > /dev/null 2>&1 &
sleep 5; pgrep -af "supervise.sh|run_all.sh" | cut -c1-100

#!/bin/bash
# Run one model to completion on shared GPUs: wait until some GPU has enough free memory, run the
# (resumable) inference script there, and retry if it dies.
# Usage: bash src/supervise.sh <model> <need_free_MiB> <batch_size>
MODEL=$1; NEED=$2; BS=$3; NAME=$(basename $MODEL)
attempt() { # extra args for run_inference.py
  while true; do
    read GPU FREE < <(nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,memory.free --format=csv,noheader,nounits | tr -d ',' | sort -k2 -n -r | head -1)
    if [ "$FREE" -ge "$NEED" ]; then
      echo "$(date +%T) $NAME: launching on GPU $GPU ($FREE MiB free): $*" >> logs/supervise.log
      CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=$GPU python src/run_inference.py --model $MODEL --batch-size $BS "$@" >> logs/run_${NAME}.log 2>&1 && return 0
      echo "$(date +%T) $NAME: run failed, retrying" >> logs/supervise.log
    fi
    sleep 45
  done
}
attempt --conditions direct cot
attempt --conditions cot2 --limit 100
echo "$(date +%T) $NAME: ALL DONE" >> logs/supervise.log
EOF

Base directory for this skill: /tmp/claude-25919/bundled-skills/2.1.293/a53c9481d4b8cbeb51a60813d28539db/dataviz

# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values - touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe - run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure - do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job - magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). -> `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) - each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. -> `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette - run the script, don't reason about Delta E.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,...>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory - or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, >=8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. -> `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer - by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. -> `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For >= 2 series a legend is always present and <= 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box - the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** - its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout - open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** - it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue - it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale -> two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake - see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light->dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD Delta E >= 8 is the
  target (OKLab ×100); 6-8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL - full-color readers can't tell the
  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead - see check 4. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view - it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for >= 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** - values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance - every value filled in - is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical - steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

## Reference files

| File | What it answers |
|------|-----------------|
| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |
| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |
| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |
| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |
| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of - build each in plain HTML |
| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong - check every chart against this** |
| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** - every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |
| `scripts/validate_palette.js` | Runnable six-checks validator (run it; don't eyeball) |

"""Analyse direct-vs-CoT results: accuracy tables, paired statistics, scale trends, robustness, figures.

All correctness values are RE-SCORED here from the saved raw outputs with src/scoring.py, so the
numbers never depend on which scoring version was live during inference.

Usage: python src/analyze.py   (reads results/model_outputs/*.jsonl, writes results/*.csv|json, figures/*.png)
"""
import glob
import json
import os
import sys

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy.stats import binomtest
from statsmodels.stats.multitest import multipletests

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(__file__))
from scoring import extract_answer, score  # noqa: E402

SEED = 42
N_BOOT = 10000
PARAMS_B = {  # parameter counts (billions) from the model cards
    "Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct": 0.49, "Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct": 1.54, "Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct": 3.09,
    "Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct": 7.61, "Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct": 14.7,
}
MODELS = list(PARAMS_B)
SHORT = {m: m.replace("Qwen2.5-", "").replace("-Instruct", "") for m in MODELS}
TASKS = ["ag_news", "sst2", "triviaqa", "mmlu_recall", "bbh_logical_deduction", "proofwriter",
         "gsm8k", "synthetic_arithmetic"]
CATS = ["pattern_matching", "factual_recall", "logical_deduction", "arithmetic"]
CAT_LABEL = {"pattern_matching": "Pattern matching", "factual_recall": "Factual recall",
             "logical_deduction": "Logical deduction", "arithmetic": "Arithmetic"}
# Hypothesised band for delta (pp) per category.
H_BAND = {"pattern_matching": (-15, -5), "factual_recall": (-15, -5),
          "logical_deduction": (10, 25), "arithmetic": (10, 25)}

# Plot styling (categorical hues in fixed order; diverging blue/orange with neutral midpoint).
CAT_COLOR = {"pattern_matching": "#2a78d6", "factual_recall": "#eb6834",
             "logical_deduction": "#1baf7a", "arithmetic": "#eda100"}
INK, MUTED, GRID, SURFACE = "#0b0b0b", "#898781", "#e1e0d9", "#fcfcfb"
plt.rcParams.update({"figure.facecolor": SURFACE, "axes.facecolor": SURFACE, "axes.edgecolor": "#c3c2b7",
                     "axes.labelcolor": "#52514e", "xtick.color": MUTED, "ytick.color": MUTED,
                     "text.color": INK, "axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False,
                     "axes.grid": True, "grid.color": GRID, "grid.linewidth": 0.6, "font.size": 10,
                     "savefig.dpi": 160, "savefig.bbox": "tight"})


def load():
    """Load all model outputs, re-score them, and return a long dataframe."""
    items = {r["id"]: r for r in map(json.loads, open("datasets/processed/tasks.jsonl"))}
    rows = []
    for path in sorted(glob.glob("results/model_outputs/*.jsonl")):
        for r in map(json.loads, open(path)):
            ans, has_marker = extract_answer(r["output"], r["condition"])
            r["answer"], r["has_marker"] = ans, has_marker
            r["correct"] = score(items[r["id"]], ans)
            r["model"] = r["model"].split("/")[-1]
            rows.append(r)
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows).drop_duplicates(["model", "id", "condition"])
    return df, items


def paired(df, model, cond_a="direct", cond_b="cot", ids=None):
    """Wide per-item table (columns: task, a, b) for one model and two conditions."""
    d = df[df.model == model]
    a = d[d.condition == cond_a].set_index("id")
    b = d[d.condition == cond_b].set_index("id")
    common = a.index.intersection(b.index)
    if ids is not None:
        common = common.intersection(ids)
    return pd.DataFrame({"task": a.loc[common, "task"], "category": a.loc[common, "category"],
                         "a": a.loc[common, "correct"], "b": b.loc[common, "correct"]})


def mcnemar_exact(a, b):
    """Two-sided exact McNemar test on paired binary outcomes."""
    n01, n10 = int(((a == 0) & (b == 1)).sum()), int(((a == 1) & (b == 0)).sum())
    return 1.0 if n01 + n10 == 0 else binomtest(n01, n01 + n10, 0.5).pvalue


def boot_delta(w, rng, n_boot=N_BOOT):
    """Bootstrap distribution of the (b - a) accuracy difference in pp.

    If several tasks are present the statistic is the macro-average of the per-task deltas and the
    resampling is stratified by task."""
    out = np.zeros(n_boot)
    groups = [g[["a", "b"]].to_numpy() for _, g in w.groupby("task")]
    for g in groups:
        idx = rng.integers(0, len(g), size=(n_boot, len(g)))
        out += (g[idx, 1].mean(1) - g[idx, 0].mean(1)) * 100 / len(groups)
    return out


def summarize(w, rng):
    """Point estimate, CI, McNemar p, harm and fix rates for a paired table."""
    per_task = w.groupby("task")[["a", "b"]].mean() * 100
    delta = float((per_task["b"] - per_task["a"]).mean())
    bd = boot_delta(w, rng)
    right, wrong = w[w.a == 1], w[w.a == 0]
    return dict(n=len(w), acc_direct=float(per_task["a"].mean()), acc_cot=float(per_task["b"].mean()),
                delta=delta, ci_lo=float(np.percentile(bd, 2.5)), ci_hi=float(np.percentile(bd, 97.5)),
                rel_delta_pct=float(100 * delta / max(per_task["a"].mean(), 1e-9)),
                p_mcnemar=mcnemar_exact(w.a, w.b),
                harm_rate=float(100 * (right.b == 0).mean()) if len(right) else np.nan,

def load():
    """Load all model outputs, re-score them, and return a long dataframe."""
    items = {r["id"]: r for r in map(json.loads, open("datasets/processed/tasks.jsonl"))}

    """Two-sided exact McNemar test on paired binary outcomes."""
    n01, n10 = int(((a == 0) & (b == 1)).sum()), int(((a == 1) & (b == 0)).sum())
    return 1.0 if n01 + n10 == 0 else binomtest(n01, n01 + n10, 0.5).pvalue

    out = np.zeros(n_boot)
    groups = [g[["a", "b"]].to_numpy() for _, g in w.groupby("task")]
    for g in groups:
        idx = rng.integers(0, len(g), size=(n_boot, len(g)))

            s, _ = summarize(w[w.category == c], rng)
            sens_rows.append(dict(model=m, category=c, n_kept=s["n"], delta_clean=s["delta"],
                                  ci_lo=s["ci_lo"], ci_hi=s["ci_hi"]))
    SENS = pd.DataFrame(sens_rows).merge(C[["model", "category", "delta", "n"]], on=["model", "category"])
    SENS.to_csv("results/sensitivity_clean_cot.csv", index=False)
    print("\n== SENSITIVITY (well-formed CoT outputs only) ==\n", SENS.round(2).to_string(index=False))

    # ---- 5. Prompt robustness: second CoT wording on the 100-item-per-task subset -------------
    rob_rows = []
    for m in models:
        ids2 = pd.Index(df[(df.model == m) & (df.condition == "cot2")]["id"])
        if len(ids2) == 0:
            continue
        w1, w2 = paired(df, m, "direct", "cot", ids2), paired(df, m, "direct", "cot2", ids2)
        for c in CATS:
            s1, _ = summarize(w1[w1.category == c], rng)
            s2, _ = summarize(w2[w2.category == c], rng)
            rob_rows.append(dict(model=m, category=c, n=s1["n"], delta_cot=s1["delta"], delta_cot2=s2["delta"],
                                 cot2_ci_lo=s2["ci_lo"], cot2_ci_hi=s2["ci_hi"]))
    R = pd.DataFrame(rob_rows)
    if len(R):
        R["same_sign"] = np.sign(R.delta_cot) == np.sign(R.delta_cot2)
        R.to_csv("results/robustness_cot2.csv", index=False)
        print("\n== ROBUSTNESS (CoT wording 2, same items) ==\n", R.round(2).to_string(index=False))
        print("sign agreement:", R.same_sign.mean().round(3), "| corr of deltas:",
              np.corrcoef(R.delta_cot, R.delta_cot2)[0, 1].round(3))

    # ---- 6. Figures --------------------------------------------------------------------------
    xs = [PARAMS_B[m] for m in models]
    # Fig 1: delta vs scale per category (small multiples, shared y axis, hypothesised band shaded)
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 4, figsize=(14, 3.6), sharey=True)
    for ax, c in zip(axes, CATS):
        d = C[C.category == c].set_index("model").loc[models]
        lo, hi = H_BAND[c]
        ax.axhspan(lo, hi, color="#f0efec", zorder=0, label="hypothesised range")
        ax.axhline(0, color=MUTED, lw=1)
        ax.errorbar(xs, d.delta, yerr=[d.delta - d.ci_lo, d.ci_hi - d.delta], color=CAT_COLOR[c], lw=2,
                    marker="o", ms=7, capsize=3, mec=SURFACE, mew=1.5, label="CoT − direct (95% CI)")
        for xv, yv in zip(xs, d.delta):
            ax.annotate(f"{yv:+.0f}", (xv, yv), textcoords="offset points", xytext=(0, 9), ha="center", fontsize=9)
        ax.set_xscale("log")
        ax.set_xticks(xs)
        ax.set_xticklabels([SHORT[m] for m in models])
        ax.minorticks_off()
        ax.set_title(CAT_LABEL[c], loc="left", fontsize=11, fontweight="bold")
        ax.set_xlabel("Qwen2.5-Instruct size (parameters)")
    axes[0].set_ylabel("Accuracy change from CoT (pp)")
    axes[0].legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8, loc="upper left")
    fig.suptitle("Chain-of-thought effect by task category and model size", x=0.01, ha="left", fontsize=13)
    fig.savefig("figures/delta_by_category_scale.png")
    plt.close(fig)

    # Fig 2: heatmap of delta, model x task (diverging, neutral midpoint)
    from matplotlib.colors import LinearSegmentedColormap, TwoSlopeNorm
    P = T.pivot(index="task", columns="model", values="delta").loc[TASKS, models]
    Sg = T.pivot(index="task", columns="model", values="sig").loc[TASKS, models]
    cmap = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list("div", ["#c2491d", "#f0efec", "#1c5cab"])
    vmax = float(np.abs(P.to_numpy()).max())
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.5, 4.6))
    im = ax.imshow(P.to_numpy(), cmap=cmap, norm=TwoSlopeNorm(0, -vmax, vmax), aspect="auto")
    ax.set_xticks(range(len(models)), [SHORT[m] for m in models])
    ax.set_yticks(range(len(TASKS)), [f"{t}  ({CAT_LABEL[items[next(i for i in items if items[i]['task'] == t)]['category']]})" for t in TASKS])
    ax.grid(False)
    for i in range(len(TASKS)):
        for j in range(len(models)):
            v = P.iloc[i, j]
            ax.text(j, i, f"{v:+.0f}" + ("*" if Sg.iloc[i, j] != "n.s." else ""), ha="center", va="center",
                    color="white" if abs(v) > 0.55 * vmax else INK, fontsize=10)
    fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, label="CoT − direct accuracy (pp)")
    ax.set_xlabel("Qwen2.5-Instruct size")
    ax.set_title("CoT accuracy change per task (* = Holm-significant, α=0.05)", loc="left", fontsize=11)
    fig.savefig("figures/delta_heatmap.png")
    plt.close(fig)

    # Fig 3: harm rate and fix rate by category and scale (two panels, one measure each)
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 3.8))
    for ax, key, title in zip(axes, ["harm_rate", "fix_rate"],
                              ["Harm rate: P(CoT wrong | direct right)", "Fix rate: P(CoT right | direct wrong)"]):
        for c in CATS:
            d = C[C.category == c].set_index("model").loc[models]
            ax.plot(xs, d[key], color=CAT_COLOR[c], lw=2, marker="o", ms=7, mec=SURFACE, mew=1.5, label=CAT_LABEL[c])
        ax.set_xscale("log")
        ax.set_xticks(xs)
        ax.set_xticklabels([SHORT[m] for m in models])
        ax.minorticks_off()
        ax.set_ylim(0, 100)
        ax.set_ylabel("% of items")
        ax.set_xlabel("Qwen2.5-Instruct size")
        ax.set_title(title, loc="left", fontsize=11)
    axes[0].legend(frameon=False, fontsize=9)
    fig.savefig("figures/harm_fix_rates.png")
    plt.close(fig)

    # Fig 4: absolute accuracy, direct vs CoT, per task (small multiples)
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 4, figsize=(14, 6), sharey=True)
    for ax, t in zip(axes.T.ravel(), TASKS):
        d = T[T.task == t].set_index("model").loc[models]
        ax.plot(xs, d.acc_direct, color="#52514e", lw=2, marker="o", ms=6, mec=SURFACE, mew=1.5, label="Direct")
        ax.plot(xs, d.acc_cot, color="#2a78d6", lw=2, marker="s", ms=6, mec=SURFACE, mew=1.5, label="CoT")
        ax.set_xscale("log")
        ax.set_xticks(xs)
        ax.set_xticklabels([SHORT[m] for m in models], fontsize=8)
        ax.minorticks_off()
        ax.set_ylim(0, 100)
        ax.set_title(f"{t}", loc="left", fontsize=10, fontweight="bold")
    for ax in axes[:, 0]:
        ax.set_ylabel("Accuracy (%)")
    axes[0, 0].legend(frameon=False, fontsize=9)
    fig.suptitle("Accuracy by task: direct answer vs chain-of-thought (columns = categories: pattern, recall, logic, arithmetic)",
                 x=0.01, ha="left", fontsize=12)
    fig.savefig("figures/accuracy_by_task.png")
    plt.close(fig)

    json.dump(dict(seed=SEED, n_boot=N_BOOT, models=models, n_rows=int(len(df))), open("results/analysis_config.json", "w"), indent=2)
    print("\nwrote results/*.csv and figures/*.png")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
